transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you—what has been bothering you lately that brought you in to see me today?

My mood has been all over the place for months—either I feel weirdly “high” and on edge or I get really snappy over the smallest things. It’s starting to mess up my relationships and I’m arguing with people a lot more than I used to.

Do these mood changes come in clear episodes where you feel very different for days or weeks at a time with more energy or less need for sleep, or have you felt emotionally up and down like this almost all the time for as long as you can remember?

It’s really been more of a new pattern over about the last 10 months, not something I’ve had my whole life. I get these stretches that last at least several days—sometimes longer—where I’m really up and wired with tons of energy and don’t seem to need much sleep, and then other stretches where I crash and feel low and drained.

During your ‘up and wired’ periods, do you ever feel so confident or driven that you do clearly risky things (like overspending, driving dangerously, using more substances, or starting big projects you can’t finish) or get into serious trouble at work, school, or in relationships because of your behavior?

Yeah, I definitely get more reckless in those times. I’ve run up my credit card on stuff I don’t need, taken on way too many projects at work that I can’t realistically finish, and I’ve hooked up impulsively a few times, which has caused arguments and tension in my relationship.

During your ‘up and wired’ periods, have you ever had times when you felt so extremely energized, important, or out of control that you lost touch with reality—like believing things others said weren’t true, hearing or seeing things others couldn’t, or needing to be in the hospital or emergency room?

No, it’s never gotten to that point. I don’t see or hear things that aren’t there, and I haven’t believed anything totally out of touch with reality or needed to go to the ER or be hospitalized during those times.

Outside of those ‘up’ and ‘crash’ periods, do you spend long stretches of time feeling mainly tense, worried, or on edge most days, or are your problems with anxiety mostly tied to those mood swings you described?

I’m not anxious all the time in between; it’s mostly tied to those mood swings. When I’m “up” I feel more wired and on edge, and when I’m down I worry a lot more, but in the middle I don’t notice constant anxiety.

During your ‘crash’ periods, do you ever feel depressed most of the day for at least two weeks in a row with clear problems functioning (like missing work, not getting out of bed, or losing interest in almost everything), or do those low phases tend to be shorter or less severe than that?

Yeah, the lows can definitely last at least a couple of weeks where I feel down pretty much all day, most days. During those times I struggle to get out of bed, I’ve missed work or just gone through the motions, and I lose interest in almost everything, including seeing people.

When you’re in those ‘up and wired’ periods, how long do they usually last at their most intense, and do other people clearly notice you’re acting very differently or say you seem like a different person during those times?

When they’re really intense, they usually last around a week or so, sometimes a bit longer before I start to crash. People around me definitely notice—my partner and coworkers say I’m talking a mile a minute, taking on too much, and seem way more amped up and irritable than my usual self.
During your lowest periods, have you ever felt so depressed or hopeless that you seriously thought about hurting yourself, made a specific plan, or attempted to end your life?

Yeah, during the worst lows I’ve definitely had times where I wished I just wouldn’t wake up and thought a lot about wanting to die. I’ve also had moments with strong urges to do something like step into traffic, and I’ve thought through specific ways I might kill myself, but I haven’t actually gone through with an attempt.

Have you ever had a period of at least a year where your mood was mostly stable, without clear ‘up’ or ‘crash’ episodes, or have these mood swings been happening fairly continuously without long stable stretches since they started 10 months ago?

Since this started about 10 months ago, it’s been pretty continuous ups and downs without any long stable stretch. I might have a few days here and there where I feel a bit more “normal,” but nothing like weeks or months of feeling like my old self.

Before these mood episodes began 10 months ago, did you start or change any medications, drugs, or alcohol use (including antidepressants, stimulants, or heavy cannabis/alcohol) that seemed to trigger or worsen these ups and downs?

I didn’t start or change any medications around that time—no antidepressants, stimulants, or anything like that. My drinking and any recreational stuff have been pretty much the same as before, so I don’t think anything like that triggered it.

There is no history of psychotic symptoms, no substance/medication trigger, and no long stable euthymic periods since onset 10 months ago. The elevated periods sound more consistent with hypomanic episodes (no psychosis, no hospitalization, but clear change and impairment), which points toward a bipolar spectrum diagnosis with current depressive episode. Under ICD-10, this makes a current depressive episode in bipolar disorder (F31.3) still plausible, but we must also consider a code reflecting a bipolar course where the most recent episode may be hypomanic or where the pattern is not yet fully characterized (F31.1 as a proxy for a non-psychotic bipolar presentation with recent elevated mood). Because the information does not yet clearly distinguish whether the most recent episode is definitively a moderate depressive episode versus a mixed or hypomanic state in a bipolar course, I have expanded the candidate list to include both F31.1 and F31.3. Further questioning is still needed to clarify exact symptom counts, duration, functional impairment for the elevated episodes, and whether the current state is primarily depressed or mixed, so the list is not final.
